ai.description: *Kaloula ghoshi* is a stout, 40–50 mm frog with a dark brown to blackish body and yellow-spotted flanks. It features a rounded snout, short limbs, and distinct, shovel-shaped metatarsal tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kaloula ghoshi* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid yellow-orange mottling on the belly and limbs, which contrasts sharply with the plain or duller undersides of other Indian *Kaloula* species.
ai.habitat: The Andaman Bullfrog inhabits tropical moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found in leaf litter near water bodies at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Bullfrog is primarily nocturnal and terrestrial, emerging from its underground burrows during the monsoon season to forage for insects and breed in pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kaloula ghoshi* is an explosive breeder that lays eggs in temporary rain pools during the monsoon season (June–August). Clutch size details remain largely undocumented.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kaloula ghoshi* is endemic to the Andaman Islands, specifically found in the South and Middle Andaman districts within low-elevation tropical forest habitats.
ai.callDescription: The Andaman Bullfrog produces a series of short, low-pitched, pulsed "oops" sounds, typically heard while calling from shallow, rain-filled pools in forest habitats.
